---
title: Write a script with TypeScript
description: Write a TypeScript script that saves a note in your library and lists the latest ones, using a key that reaches notes and nothing else.
---

- **You'll build** Standup, a TypeScript script that saves a note for the day and lists your last five.
- **You need** your own Marfa instance, with the CLI signed in to it, as the [Quickstart](/quickstart) leaves you, at `http://localhost:8600`. You also need Node.js 22.18 or later.
- **You'll have** a script that runs with a key of its own, which can read and write notes and nothing else.

The CLI's sign-in stays in your keychain, on your computer. A script carries a **key** instead: a secret that names exactly which types it can read or write. It works from any computer that can reach your instance, such as a server or a scheduled job.

<Steps paged>
<Step>

### Make a key for the script

Ask the CLI for a key that can write notes:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa keys create --label "Standup script" --source standup --type-permission core.note=write
```

```text
marfa_k1_…
key 01a1f184-1bed-74ae-afc6-32fc15c97ef3 (Standup script); the plaintext is shown once, keep it now
  core.note  Read and edit
```

</Terminal>

The first line is the key. **Copy it now**: Marfa shows it only once and keeps only a hash of it.

`--type-permission core.note=write` lets the key read and write notes, the type `core.note`, and nothing else. `--source standup` names where the notes it writes come from, so an app can show and filter them by it.

</Step>
<Step>

### Create the project

Make a folder for the script, and install the [TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk) with TypeScript itself:

```bash
mkdir standup && cd standup
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm install @withmarfa/client
npm install --save-dev typescript @types/node
```

Node.js runs a `.ts` file by removing its types, so the script needs no build step. TypeScript checks the types. Give it a `tsconfig.json`:

```json title="tsconfig.json"
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "module": "nodenext",
    "target": "esnext",
    "types": ["node"],
    "strict": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "erasableSyntaxOnly": true,
    "verbatimModuleSyntax": true
  }
}
```

Then tell the script where your instance is and which key to send, in the same terminal:

```bash
export MARFA_API_URL=http://localhost:8600
export MARFA_API_KEY=marfa_k1_…
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Save a note

Create `standup.ts`. It makes a client for your instance, then saves what you type after the command as a note, titled with today's date and tagged `standup`:

```ts title="standup.ts"
import { createClient } from "@withmarfa/client";

const { MARFA_API_URL, MARFA_API_KEY } = process.env;
if (!MARFA_API_URL || !MARFA_API_KEY) {
  throw new Error("Set MARFA_API_URL and MARFA_API_KEY first.");
}
const marfa = createClient({ baseUrl: MARFA_API_URL, credential: MARFA_API_KEY });

const text = process.argv.slice(2).join(" ");
if (text) {
  const today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
  const { data, error } = await marfa.POST("/items", {
    body: {
      type: "core.note",
      properties: { title: `Standup ${today}`, body: text },
      tags: ["standup"],
    },
  });
  if (error) throw new Error(`${error.error.code}: ${error.error.message}`);
  console.log(`Saved ${data.item.id}, version ${data.item.version}`);
}
```

Every call returns `data` when it works and `error` when Marfa refuses. **Check `error` first**: after that, TypeScript knows the shape of `data`. Branch on `error.error.code`, which stays the same, rather than the message.

Run it with a line for today:

<Terminal>

```bash
node standup.ts "Shipped the export fix, reviewing the importer next"
```

```text
Saved 01a1f184-1ca3-7014-a945-ebd0bce70faf, version 1
```

</Terminal>

The note is an **item**, with an ID and a version that rises each time it changes. Run `marfa items list --type core.note --tag standup` to see it from the CLI.

</Step>
<Step>

### List your notes

Add a read to the end of `standup.ts`. It asks for the five newest notes tagged `standup`:

```ts title="standup.ts"
const { data, error } = await marfa.GET("/items", {
  params: { query: { type: "core.note", tags: "standup", limit: 5 } },
});
if (error) throw new Error(`${error.error.code}: ${error.error.message}`);
for (const note of data.data) {
  if ("id" in note) console.log(`${note.properties.title}: ${note.properties.body}`);
}
```

The `"id" in note` check tells TypeScript each entry is an item: a list that asks for metadata answers each item with its metadata instead. Check the types, then run the script with nothing after it, so it only reads:

<Terminal>

```bash
npx tsc
node standup.ts
```

```text
Standup 2026-11-19: Shipped the export fix, reviewing the importer next
```

</Terminal>

`npx tsc` prints nothing when the types are right. Save another line and run it again: the list shows the newest note first.

</Step>
<Step>

### See what the key can't do

In `standup.ts`, change `type: "core.note"` in the write to `type: "core.task"`, and run it:

<Terminal>

```bash
node standup.ts "Review the importer"
```

```text
Error: type_not_permitted: No access to type "core.task"
```

</Terminal>

Marfa refuses the write with `403 type_not_permitted`, because the key holds only notes. The refusal's `details.grant` names the type and the level the request needed. **A key reaches only what you gave it**, so a script that leaks its key exposes your notes and nothing else.

Change the type back to `core.note`. To let the script write tasks too, make a new key that names both types: signed in with `marfa login`, `marfa keys update` can take access away from a key but never give it more. A source belongs to one live key, so revoke the first key before you reuse `standup`:

```bash
marfa keys revoke 01a1f184-1bed-74ae-afc6-32fc15c97ef3
marfa keys create --label "Standup script" --source standup \
  --type-permission core.note=write --type-permission core.task=write
```

Put the new key in `MARFA_API_KEY`. [Manage keys](/run/manage-keys) covers expiry, narrowing and revoking a key.
